best_for: Windows users who want Git, a shell, a credential helper and a basic GUI from one installer.

points.title: More than the command
points.text: The Windows installer includes Git Bash (a shell), Git GUI, right-click entries in Explorer, and Git Credential Manager for signing in to hosted repositories.

points.title: It is a command-line tool first
points.text: Git itself is commands, not a full visual tool. Graphical clients and editors sit on top of it; Git GUI is the only graphical piece in the box.

points.title: Not an MSI
points.text: The project publishes an .exe installer and a portable package, but no MSI. Fleet deployments that need MSI have to wrap the installer themselves.

points.title: Dropped old Windows
points.text: From version 2.47 Git for Windows stopped supporting Windows 7, 8, XP and Server 2003, and it no longer ships 32-bit builds. Only x64 and Arm64 are listed here.

points.title: Version numbers carry a fourth part
points.text: 2.56.0.4 means Git 2.56.0 plus the fourth Windows-specific revision. The extra number changes when the Windows packaging is fixed without a new Git release.

points.title: winget packages are not the project's
points.text: The project's FAQ says the winget and Chocolatey packages are not maintained by the Git for Windows team. The installer itself comes from the project's own download.

points.title: On Mac and Linux
points.text: There is no Git for Windows equivalent here. Mac users get Git through Homebrew, MacPorts or Xcode's command line tools; Linux users install it from their distribution, for example with apt-get install git on Debian and Ubuntu.
